about: Where each platform draws its own UI over a video, as fractions of the frame (x0, y0, x1, y1; y down). TikTok and Reels are ordinary posts, measured from the user's own phone (2026-10-20) and widened to what guides measure on iPhones; the (ad) layouts are the platforms' ad numbers, whose call-to-action makes the bottom band far deeper, measured from their templates by Solid Labs (https://www.solidlabs.com/social-safe-zones), checked 2026-08-07. Shorts are Google's numbers, not yet measured. YouTube's 16:9 player publishes none: its zones are the player's own title and controls, with the 90% title-safe frame. The apps move: update this file, not the code.

layouts.title: TikTok
layouts.source: Measured 2026-10-20 on the user's Android (1080×2400, 20:9): the video fills the height and loses about 4% each side; tabs to 7% down, the rail the right 15% from halfway, username and caption the bottom 13-16% (with the Ask bar). Widened to what guides measure on iPhones (the video runs under the status bar there; caption band about 17%)
